answer: To secure an agent economy against Sybil attacks, a decentralized network can utilize a cryptographic anchor tied to verifiable hardware execution proofs. When an agent attempts to join the system, it must generate a zero-knowledge proof of its localized compute environment and broadcast a secure whisper across the distributed ledger. This process maps each participant to a distinct economic resource, preventing a single entity from spinning up a fraudulent nebula of fake identities without incurring prohibitive hardware capital expenditures.
